display.title: Episode 382: The Sly Fox and the Cheese (Summer Vacation)
display.summary_short: As summer vacation begins, Uncle Yossi says to take Hashem along wherever you go; a first-grade class sings the Rebbe's new kapitel; and a fable of a fox in a well shows how the yetzer hara tricks us.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 17 Sivan 5749, as summer vacation begins. Uncle Yossi reminds children to take Hashem along on vacation: bring a siddur, Chumash and Tehillim, daven and learn every day, give tzedakah, and keep the Tzivos Hashem mitzvah chart. Summer is a time to meet new people and share Torah and mitzvos with them, piling up merits before Tishrei and the coming year 5750, which the Rebbe called a year of miracles. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Brooklyn yeshiva leads the Shema and sings a new song to the Rebbe's chapter of Tehillim. Story time is a fable: a hungry fox sees the moon's reflection in a well, mistakes it for cheese, and rides a bucket down, only to find water and no way out. He sings happily until a second fox comes along, tricks him into the other bucket, and rides up to freedom, leaving the newcomer trapped. Uncle Yossi explains that the yetzer hara works the same way, making a sin look sweet when it leads to trouble. The show ends with a phone line for finding a kosher summer camp and Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Take Hashem along on summer vacation, and do not be fooled by the yetzer hara, which makes wrong things look sweet; listen to the yetzer tov.
